title: Expose Epi Curve in upload launch-view options
observed_behavior: While implementing direct-launch coverage for Epi Curve, the File Settings `default-view` select did not offer `Epi Curve` as a launch option, so the uploaded fixture could not be configured to open there directly even though launch-view handling elsewhere recognizes `Epi Curve`.
intended_behavior: File Settings should expose `Epi Curve` as a valid launch target so uploaded node+link data can land directly in an interactive Epi Curve without requiring a post-launch view switch.
cause_summary: The launch-view dropdown in Files originally omitted `Epi Curve` even though the top-level view logic already handled it as a recognized tab name.
fix_summary: Added `Epi Curve` to the File Settings `default-view` options and re-enabled the maintained direct-launch Epi journey.
notes: Closed after enabling the launch option in File Settings and verifying the direct-launch Cypress path against uploaded node+link data.

title: Remove inert Epi Curve PNG quality control
observed_behavior: While implementing the remaining Epi export coverage, the PNG Quality slider was present in the dialog and bound to `SelectedNetworkExportQualityVariable`, but `exportVisualization()` still called `saveSvgAsPng()` without `encoderOptions`, so changing the slider could not affect PNG output.
intended_behavior: Changing PNG Quality should influence the export encoder settings, or the control should be removed or disabled so the dialog does not present an inert option.
cause_summary: The export dialog originally exposed `#network-export-quality` even though the PNG export path could not honor it.
fix_summary: Removed the unsupported PNG quality slider from the Epi export dialog and added a maintained Cypress assertion that advanced export no longer exposes the inert control.
notes: Closed by removing the misleading control instead of preserving a no-op UI surface.

title: Release processing modal after Epi direct launch
observed_behavior: After enabling `Epi Curve` in File Settings, direct launch still stalled behind the shared Processing Files dialog even though the Epi tab had opened and the component was interactive.
intended_behavior: Launching directly into Epi Curve should dismiss the shared processing modal once the Epi view is mounted even when 2D Network is never opened first.
cause_summary: TimelineComponent did not call `setNetworkRendered(true)`, so the global loading-modal lifecycle kept waiting on a render signal that other non-2D views already emitted.
fix_summary: Added an Epi-specific render completion signal in `TimelineComponent` and updated the direct-launch spec to assert session counts instead of 2D-only metric badges.
notes: Closed after the direct-launch Epi journey completed end to end without a stuck processing modal.

title: Clear Epi chart state when date filter is None
observed_behavior: While extending maintained controls coverage, setting the active Epi date field to `None` left the previous bars and axes rendered on screen instead of clearing the chart. The same stale-SVG behavior reproduced after clearing every selected multi-date field.
intended_behavior: Resetting date selections to `None` should clear the current Epi rendering so the view does not display stale histogram output for a field that is no longer selected.
cause_summary: Both `refresh()` and `refreshMulti()` returned early on the no-date paths before clearing `#epiCurveSVG`, so stale bars and axes persisted from the prior render.
fix_summary: Moved the SVG clear step ahead of the no-date early returns in both refresh paths and added maintained Cypress coverage for single-date and multi-date resets to `None`.
notes: Closed after the new controls journey verified that bars and axes disappear when active date selections are cleared.

title: Keep Lineage-colored Epi isolated from global State color table
observed_behavior: Updating the global node color table for State could change colors in an Epi Curve that was colored by Lineage rather than Node Color.
intended_behavior: Global node color table edits should only affect Epi colors when Epi Curve is explicitly colored by Node Color; independent Epi categorical fields should keep their own palette.
cause_summary: The regression path was a global node-color update event reaching Epi even when `epiCurve-stackColorBy` was an independent field.
fix_summary: The Epi update path now stays scoped to the Node Color mode, and the maintained Cypress spec edits the global State table while Epi is colored by Lineage to guard that behavior.
notes: Closed after the Epi styling journey verified B.1.617.2 remains blue after the Colorado State color is changed to black and after the node color table is floated.
